target.title: fix(codex): bound Codex CLI auth file read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveCodexCliAuthFileApiKeyCacheKey` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-bridge.ts` reads the entire Codex CLI auth file (`CODEX_HOME/auth.json`) via unbounded `fsSync.readFileSync(resolveCodexCliAuthFilePath(env), "utf8")` solely to fingerprint an API-key cache key. The path is derived from the external `CODEX_HOME` env var (or `~/.codex/auth.json`), so a misconfigured or oversized auth file triggers an unbounded memory read just to compute a `CODEX_AUTH_JSON:sha256:...` cache identity.

The provider-local ADC credential copy of this exact logic in `extensions/anthropic-vertex/region.ts` was already bounded with `tryReadSecretFileSync` + a 1 MiB limit in #109260 ("reject oversized credential files in remaining readers"); this standalone sync Codex CLI auth-file reader is a duplicate that sweep missed.

Mirror the region.ts bound: replace the unbounded `readFileSync` with `tryReadSecretFileSync(..., { maxBytes: 1 MiB, rejectHardlinks: false })`, guarded by `if (!text) return undefined`. `tryReadSecretFileSync` throws `FsSafeError` on oversize; the guard + existing `try/catch` return `undefined` (the file is treated as unreadable, same as a missing/corrupt auth file) instead of slurping it into memory. Presence/cache-key semantics are unchanged for normal-sized files.

## Evidence

- The fix replaces `fsSync.readFileSync(resolveCodexCliAuthFilePath(env), "utf8")` with `tryReadSecretFileSync(resolveCodexCliAuthFilePath(env), "Codex CLI auth file", { maxBytes: 1 MiB, rejectHardlinks: false })` + an `if (!text) return undefined` guard, mirroring the bound in `extensions/anthropic-vertex/region.ts:116` (#109260). The now-unused `import fsSync from "node:fs"` is removed (`fs` from `node:fs/promises`, used by the async key fetch, stays).
- New regression test `rejects an oversized Codex CLI auth.json instead of slurping it into memory`: writes a valid 1 MiB+ JSON auth file to a temp `CODEX_HOME` and asserts `resolveCodexAppServerFallbackApiKeyCacheKey` returns `undefined` (bound rejects). The existing `includes Codex CLI api-key auth.json in fallback app-server cache keys` test confirms a normal-sized auth file still yields a `CODEX_AUTH_JSON:sha256:...` key (no regression).
- Local vitest run (Node v22.22.3, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-bridge.test.ts`):
  - `-t "Codex CLI api-key auth.json"`: 3 passed | 74 skipped.
  - `-t "oversized Codex CLI auth.json"`: 1 passed | 76 skipped.
- Standalone proof (`proof-codex-cli-auth-file-bound.mts`, exercised through the exported `resolveCodexAppServerFallbackApiKeyCacheKey`):
  - Normal auth.json (43 B) -> `CODEX_AUTH_JSON:sha256:95545eab...` (preserved).
  - Oversized auth.json (2 MiB) -> `undefined` (rejected by bound); the old unbounded `readFileSync` read the entire 2 MiB file into memory.
  - `RESULT: normal read preserved = true; oversized rejected by bound = true; old code read it fully = true` -> `PASS`.
- `oxlint` on both changed files: clean (no warnings/errors).

Sibling of #109260 (same `tryReadSecretFileSync` 1 MiB bound, same unbounded-sync-readFileSync-of-a-credential-file shape); applies it to the Codex CLI auth-file reader the original sweep missed. The async `fs.readFile` key fetch in `readCodexCliAuthFileApiKey` is a separate async-read pattern (no sync bound applies) and is intentionally left out of scope, consistent with the #109260 family.
